question.prompt:
Problems \(15,\) \(16,\) and \(17\) all refer to the following:

Don’t Crowd The Isles

In the very center of the Irenic Sea lie the beautiful Nisos Isles. In \(1998\) the number of people on these islands is only \(200,\) but the population triples every \(25\) years. Queen Irene has decreed that there must be at least \(1.5\) square miles for every person living in the Isles. The total area of the Nisos Isles is \(24{,}900\) square miles.

In how many years, approximately, from \(1998\) will the population of Nisos be as much as Queen Irene has proclaimed that the islands can support?

solutions.explanation:
First find how many people the land can support. Each person needs at least \(1.5\) square miles, so the maximum supported population is
\[
24{,}900\div1.5=16{,}600.
\]
Tripling the initial population at successive \(25\)-year dates gives
\[
200\longrightarrow600\longrightarrow1800
\longrightarrow5400\longrightarrow16{,}200.
\]
Thus after \(4\times25=100\) years, the population is only \(400\) below capacity.

To estimate when capacity is actually reached, assume steady proportional growth: the population increases continuously, and equal-length time intervals multiply it by the same factor. Each half of a \(25\)-year period then has the same multiplying factor. This factor must exceed \(1.5\), because
\[
1.5\times1.5=2.25<3.
\]
Consequently, after another \(12.5\) years the population exceeds
\[
16{,}200\times1.5=24{,}300>16{,}600.
\]
Under this assumption, capacity is reached between \(100\) and \(112.5\) years. Every time in that interval is closer to \(100\) than to any other offered time, so the answer is approximately \(100\) years, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

However, the question does not specify growth between the \(25\)-year dates. For example, suppose the population stays constant between tripling jumps at elapsed years \(24,49,74,99,124,\ldots\). It still triples every \(25\) years and has exactly the populations calculated above at years \(25,50,75,100,\ldots\). But it stays at \(16{,}200\) until year \(124\), when it jumps to \(48{,}600\), first exceeding capacity. That time is closest to \(125\) years, choice D. Therefore C is conditional on the steady-growth interpretation; the wording alone does not determine a unique choice.
solutions.title: Compare capacity with repeated tripling
